patients.summary: Retired construction worker on disability with schizophrenia, type 2 diabetes, hypertension and untreated chronic hepatitis B who joined in 2019. Over seven years: iron deficiency anemia, sleep apnea, ectopic ACTH from a resected bronchial carcinoid, cervical radiculopathy, primary polydipsia, hepatitis B-associated PAN and severe finger frostbite. Records arrive with gaps.

documents.title: New patient call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Sister phoned on his behalf; he was on the line too. He wants to move his primary care here, says his old office kept changing doctors. Medicare (disability). Has an outside psychiatrist he sees for schizophrenia. Booked new patient visit 2/12 at 9:30. Records release sent to his prior practice. Asked him to bring all his medicine bottles, including over-the-counter.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily with meals
Take 1 capsule by mouth at bedtime as needed for sleep
Chew 1 tablet as needed for indigestion

procedures.procedure: Office visit, new patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
45M here to establish. Sister along for part of the visit, with his permission.

HPI: Long-standing BP and diabetes, both on pills from his last PCP. Takes lisinopril 20 daily and metformin 1000 twice a day, says he rarely misses those. Schizophrenia since his twenties; sees an outside psychiatrist every couple of months; prescribed risperidone 2 mg daily but he admits he stops it for stretches when he feels fine. Hep B found years ago on blood work; brother also carries it. Says nobody ever offered him treatment and he has never seen a liver doctor. Stomach ulcer about ten years ago, now just occasional heartburn, chews calcium carbonate for it. Main complaint today: bulge in the right groin for about a year and a half, aches when he lifts or after a long walk, goes back in when he lies down. Uses diphenhydramine some nights to sleep.

PMH: as above. PSH: none.
Meds: lisinopril 20 mg daily; metformin 1000 mg BID; risperidone 2 mg daily (intermittent); diphenhydramine 25 mg qhs prn; calcium carbonate 500 mg prn.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: father with type 2 DM and HTN. Mother with schizophrenia. Brother is a hep B carrier.
SH: Retired construction worker, on disability. Lives alone. Smoked about a pack a day for ten years, quit in 2017. No alcohol, no drugs.

Exam: well-appearing, a little guarded, answers in short sentences, linear. HEENT unremarkable. Neck supple. Heart regular rate, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no organomegaly. Right inguinal hernia, reducible, nontender, no overlying skin change; left side normal. Extremities without edema. Feet: skin intact, monofilament normal, pulses 2+.
Vitals as charted; BP at goal.

A/P:
1. Right inguinal hernia, symptomatic, reducible. Referred to general surgery to talk about elective repair. Reviewed warning signs of incarceration.
2. HTN, at goal on lisinopril. CMP.
3. Type 2 DM. A1c, lipids, urine microalbumin. Eye exam due; given optometry list.
4. Chronic hep B, never evaluated. HBsAg and LFTs today. Will revisit specialist referral once labs back.
5. Schizophrenia, outside psychiatry. Encouraged him to stay on risperidone.
6. Prevention: HCV and HIV screens today. Tdap given (none on record). PHQ-2 negative.
RTC 4 months.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Sean, your labs are back. Your A1c is 6.9, close to the goal and fine for now. Kidney and liver numbers are normal. The hepatitis B surface antigen is positive, which we expected since you have carried it for years. Hepatitis C and HIV tests are negative. Cholesterol and urine protein are fine. Nothing to change today. We'll go over the hepatitis B again at your next visit.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care practice
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Received 41 pages from his previous primary care office (2013-2018). Summary for the chart: hypertension on lisinopril 20 mg. Type 2 diabetes on metformin since 2014, A1c values mostly in the high 6s. Hepatitis B surface antigen positive on several draws, liver enzymes normal; no specialist visit documented. Schizophrenia managed by outside psychiatry. Routine labs otherwise unremarkable. Scanned under Media.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Routine DM/HTN check. Groin still aches with lifting; surgery appointment is in August, the first one they had. Taking metformin and lisinopril. Risperidone: "most days." Sleeps OK with the diphenhydramine now and then.
O: Vitals as charted. Alert, calm. Lungs clear, heart regular. Hernia unchanged, reducible. Feet intact.
A/P: DM, controlled; A1c and BMP today. HTN at goal. Hernia, surgery consult pending. Hep B: offered liver clinic referral; he wants to wait and think it over. RTC 6 months.

documents.title: General Surgery Consultation
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
Outside general surgery clinic. Date of service 8/14/2019. Reason for referral: right groin hernia.

46-year-old man with an 18-month history of a right groin bulge that aches with lifting and prolonged walking and reduces when supine. No episodes of incarceration, no bowel symptoms. History of hypertension, type 2 diabetes, chronic hepatitis B, peptic ulcer disease and schizophrenia. Medications: lisinopril, metformin, risperidone, diphenhydramine as needed, calcium carbonate as needed. No known drug allergies. Former smoker.

Exam: right indirect-type inguinal hernia, easily reducible, nontender. Left groin normal. Abdomen soft.

Impression: symptomatic reducible right inguinal hernia, suitable for elective open repair with mesh.

Plan: We discussed elective repair, its risks and recovery. Given his psychiatric history and recent lapses in his antipsychotic, we would like clearance from his psychiatrist before scheduling, so that he can manage the postoperative period and instructions. Our office will contact his psychiatry clinic. Thank you for the referral.

documents.title: Call from surgery office
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Surgical scheduler called to confirm the patient still wants the hernia repair and to ask if we had heard from psychiatry. Told them we have not. Called pt: he says his psychiatry appointment is in October and they will "sign off then." Surgery will wait for that letter.

documents.title: Outpatient Psychiatry Note
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
Outside community psychiatry clinic. Date of service 10/21/2019. Copy to primary care and to general surgery.

Reason for visit: scheduled medication follow-up; the surgical team asked us to comment on readiness for elective right inguinal hernia repair.

Interval history: Mr. Berman stopped his risperidone roughly a month ago. His sister, who came with him, says he has been hearing voices again and has told her that programs on the TV are aimed at him with hidden messages. He minimizes this. Sleep irregular. No reported violence or self-harm, no thoughts of harming himself or others on direct questioning. The hernia bothers him when he is active and he says he wants it fixed.

Medical history: hypertension and type 2 diabetes, both controlled on lisinopril and metformin; chronic hepatitis B; peptic ulcer disease; reducible inguinal hernia. Other medications: diphenhydramine 25 mg at bedtime as needed, calcium carbonate 500 mg as needed. NKDA. Family history: mother with schizophrenia; father with diabetes and hypertension; brother a hepatitis B carrier. Former smoker (quit 2017, 10 pack-years), no alcohol. Retired from construction, on disability.

Mental status: unkempt, poor eye contact, mutters to himself at times. Alert. Appears to be attending to internal stimuli. Thought process mostly goal-directed with some tangents. Insight and judgment limited. Vitals stable. Medical exam per our nurse unremarkable apart from the known groin hernia.

Metabolic monitoring today: A1c 6.8%, fasting glucose 138, creatinine 1.0, BUN 14, sodium 140, potassium 4.2.

Assessment: schizophrenia with recurrence of positive symptoms after a month off medication.

Plan: Restart risperidone 2 mg daily; reviewed side effects; sister will help with a pill box. Recheck in 4 weeks. Regarding surgery: we recommend deferring the elective repair until he has been back on medication and stable for a few months, so he can follow perioperative instructions reliably. We will update the surgeon when that is the case.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Influenza Vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Seasonal flu vaccine 0.5 mL IM left deltoid. No egg or vaccine reactions in the past. VIS given. Tolerated well. He mentioned the surgery is on hold until his psychiatrist clears him; psychiatry letter now in chart.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Back on risperidone since late October, sister fills a weekly pill box. Says the voices are "quieter." Hernia unchanged, no pain at rest; surgery waiting on psychiatry. No new complaints.
O: Vitals as charted. Calmer than in the summer, better eye contact. Heart regular, lungs clear. Hernia reducible.
A/P: DM and HTN stable, same meds; A1c and BMP drawn. Schizophrenia, back on medication, outside psychiatry following. PHQ-9 4. Hep B: still prefers to hold off on a liver referral; will keep checking LFTs. RTC 4-6 months.

documents.title: Refill request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy fax for metformin 1000 mg BID and lisinopril 20 mg daily, 90-day supply. Last visit 12/2019, labs current. Approved per protocol, sent.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

orders.reason: iron deficiency anemia with guaiac-positive stool

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Masked in-person visit.

S: About three months of getting worn out more and more, now winded walking up the hill to his building or carrying groceries up one flight. No chest pain, no racing heart, no fainting. No black stools he has noticed, no vomiting blood. Occasional heartburn, chews calcium carbonate. On risperidone "most days." Hernia unchanged.

O: Vitals as charted. Looks tired. Skin and conjunctivae pale. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Rectal: brown stool, guaiac positive. No edema.
ECG: sinus, normal.

Addendum 3:30 pm: Hgb 10.2, MCV 72. Iron 30, TIBC 450, sat 7%, ferritin 15. Iron deficiency anemia.

A/P:
1. Iron deficiency anemia, microcytic, guaiac positive, prior ulcer disease. Needs a GI look from both ends. GI referral placed. Start ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily, every other day if his stomach objects. Told him to call or go to the ED for black stools, vomiting blood, chest pain or fainting.
2. Exertional dyspnea most likely from the anemia; normal ECG. Recheck after iron.
3. DM/HTN: no changes.
Called pt with results at 3:40 pm; sister on speaker. CBC in 3 months.

documents.title: Iron instructions and GI scheduling
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Reviewed iron with pt and sister: take with water or juice, not with the calcium chews or within 2 hours of them. Stools will turn dark; red or tarry and sticky stools, or feeling faint, are reasons to call. GI office has the referral; procedures delayed by the pandemic, they will call with a date in June.

events.reason: Upper endoscopy and colonoscopy for iron deficiency anemia

medications.drug: omeprazole 40 MG Delayed Release Oral Capsule
medications.sig: Take 1 capsule by mouth daily before breakfast for 8 weeks
medications.reason: old duodenal ulcer scarring with iron deficiency

reports.text: Specimen: gastric antrum and body, cold biopsies. Gastric mucosa of antral and oxyntic type with no significant inflammation. No intestinal metaplasia, dysplasia or malignancy. Immunostain for Helicobacter organisms negative.
reports.conclusion: Benign gastric mucosa. H. pylori negative.

documents.title: EGD and Colonoscopy Report
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
Outside endoscopy center. Date of procedure 6/18/2020. Indication: iron deficiency anemia, guaiac-positive stool, remote peptic ulcer. Sedation: monitored anesthesia care. No known drug allergies.

EGD: Esophagus normal, Z-line regular. Stomach normal; biopsies from antrum and body for H. pylori. Duodenal bulb scarred and mildly deformed, consistent with old ulcer disease; no active ulcer, no blood, no visible vessel. Second part of duodenum normal.

Colonoscopy: Prep good. Advanced to the cecum, identified by the appendiceal orifice and the ileocecal valve. Normal mucosa throughout. No polyps, no masses, no blood. Retroflexion normal.

Impression: bulb deformity from prior peptic ulcer disease; otherwise normal upper and lower exam. No active bleeding source seen.

Recommendations: omeprazole 40 mg daily for 8 weeks. Continue oral iron per PCP. Await biopsies. Repeat colonoscopy in 10 years.

Addendum 6/22: biopsies benign, H. pylori negative.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Has more energy, can do the stairs without stopping. Taking iron daily with some constipation. Finishing the omeprazole from GI. No dark or bloody stools.
O: Vitals as charted. Less pale. Heart regular, lungs clear.
Scope report reviewed: old bulb scarring, normal colon, biopsies benign.
A/P: Iron deficiency anemia improving; Hgb 12.4 today (result back at noon). Continue iron. Recheck CBC and iron at the fall visit.

orders.reason: loud snoring, witnessed apneas, daytime sleepiness

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Feels well, energy back. Iron daily. Sister came along and raised something new: when she stays over at his place a few nights a week he snores loudly and she has seen him stop breathing and then gasp. He dozes off watching TV in the afternoon and admits he gets drowsy behind the wheel on longer drives. Still uses diphenhydramine some nights. Weight up a little this year.
O: Vitals as charted. Heart regular, lungs clear. Neck thick. Feet normal to monofilament.
A/P:
1. Possible obstructive sleep apnea: referral to pulmonary/sleep. Strongly advised no driving when drowsy until evaluated.
2. Iron deficiency anemia: Hgb 13.6, ferritin 52 (back this evening). Continue iron 3 more months then stop.
3. DM, HTN: labs today, no changes.
4. Flu shot given.

documents.title: Pulmonary and Sleep Medicine Consultation
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
Outside pulmonary and sleep medicine practice. Date of visit 12/10/2020. Referred by primary care.

History: 47-year-old man with schizophrenia, type 2 diabetes, hypertension and iron deficiency anemia (worked up and treated this year) referred for sleepiness. He reports he is sleepy most days and has come close to nodding off while driving several times; a few weeks ago he had a minor fender-bender he thinks was from drowsiness. His sister, who stays with him some nights, describes heavy snoring with pauses in breathing. He takes diphenhydramine on and off to fall asleep. Other medications: lisinopril 20 mg, metformin 1,000 mg BID, risperidone 2 mg (taken irregularly), calcium carbonate as needed, ferrous sulfate. NKDA. Quit smoking in 2017, 10 pack-years. No alcohol.

Exam: BMI 32. BP 145/90. Neck circumference 17 inches. Crowded oropharynx. Lungs clear. Heart regular.

Epworth Sleepiness Scale: 16/24.

Impression: high pretest probability of obstructive sleep apnea with severe subjective sleepiness.

Plan: in-laboratory polysomnography with split-night CPAP titration. We counseled him not to drive while sleepy and told him that this is a safety issue for himself and others. Weight loss would help. Follow up after the study.
